newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 11.5/12.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 11.5/12.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 11.5/12.5 percent on Friday on stable liquidity, dealers said.
They said liquidity supply was adequate despite the weekly tax payments due Friday. The central bank injected some 580 billion rupiah into the money market on Friday.
Dealers said the interbank rate was likely to decline in the afternoon because of heavy dollar selling on Friday which might induce additonal rupiah supply next week.
Overnight swap was at 1.5/1.6 and tom/next at 0.37/0.42.
Longer-term money rates were stable, with one-month and three-month money quoted at 12.875/13.00 percent and 13.75/14.00 percent, respectively.
The central bank did not offer overnight bilateral papers (SBIs), but only the longer-term ones.
It offered 6-7 day SBIs at 10.25 percent, 14-day at 11.0 percent, one-month at 12.0 percent, three at 12.75 percent, six at 13.00 and 12 at 13.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 12.63 percent, compared with 10.62 percent on Wednesday.
